Messages.Author: rdco...@gmail.com

sath...@o2.pl wrote:
> Inconnu Tutelage

Wow.

This, to my mind, represents a distinct change in design direction.
"Master, 2 pool, Search your library for a card and take it into your
hand, discard + shuffle" has been notable by its absenced from the game
ever since Jyhad became the second Deckmaster game. I'm fairly sure I
recall that in the initial discussion of the game when new it was noted
that this was intentional as well (Jyhad having been designed
deliberately to emphasise management of game resources other than card
draws; hence cards like elder library manipulating hand size more than
draws)

Anyway, back to the present: we now have clan-free, discipline free,
reusable, unrestricted deck search...Wow!

I honestly cannot think of a single deck of mine that won't be freeing
up a slot for one of these.
(well, OK, if I ever make a turbo deck or a goodnight sweet prince
deck, then probably not)

The number of times I'd have been able to lunge for an extra oust in
the end game if I'd had a Wake when needed, a stealth card when needed,
a conditioning when needed, replace the Majesty I just used... etc, etc

This combined with a card that generates a potential for an unheard of
density of rush actions in a deck makes me feel that the game is going
to be changing in some very fundamental ways in the coming months.

I'm inclined to actually purchase boosters of this set - and I've not
bought boosters for V:TES since before it was V:TES.

Its a shakeup that seems big to me, but seems to preserve the nature of
the game (I am in the "not impressed" camp regarding NoR, from a purely
conceptual stance) and add some renewed interest (new concepts, cards
that invigorate "second string" concepts)

So far only one card (breaking the wall) has struck me as "wrong" in
some way (belongs to be a malkavian card, without the excuse of
malkavian strangeness its just stupidity, IMO) and I'm a picky sod;
thats very good going.

In message <ecf0e8$vvr$1...@news.net.uni-c.dk>, FC <f...@kemi.dtu.dk> writes:
>I am sorry if I have upset you. Its just that a random draw does, in

With a random draw, is it possible that you won't draw Inconnu Tutelage,
and that you won't have a vampire you want to burn in your uncontrolled
region?

And is it possible that while you're drawing Deflection or Delaying
Tactics, your predator is using it to great effect to draw cards too?
As is your prey? You know, what with it being usable by every
Methuselah and not just the one playing it. Thus giving you two people,
in the general case, who are using it, relative to just one use for you.

The "point of the game" also includes subtle and non-obvious balancing
factors that make some cards trickier than they look. The fact that
Inconnu Tutelage is so open and usable by other Methuselahs means it's
somewhat harder to hyper-optimize your deck in a way that other
Methuselahs wouldn't be able to take advantage of most likely. An
example might be a hypothetical card that allowed all Methuselahs to get
allies or retainers from your library - a great many decks wouldn't be
able to benefit from that, while you could hyper-optimize your Shambling
Hordes deck, or your War Ghoul deck, to get a great benefit with a
relatively low risk of other people taking advantage of the same
benefit.
